statement: Set board mostly metal crops; take crop transfer ticket from world 6 shop, hand it to the bean trader, then immediately return to town.
Crop transfer ticket is obtained from the world 6 shop and used on the bean trader for the metal crop tech.
With seven trillion beans handed in then going back to town, he got hundreds of thousands of metal crops while walking into overgrowth 16/17.
Some say waiting 10-20 minutes in the mama trolls map gives more metal crops because it stacks; he hasn't tested it and goes straight to town.
His method is to return to town immediately after handing in beans to the bean trader; it gives plenty. Suggests trying the waiting variant yourself.
Not all crops need to be metal; he does one to two lines of metal crops and the rest crystal/glassy crops.
Do one-by-one tech on glassy crops: click one, go back and trade, repeat; gives roughly 40-50% extra beans for night market.
Keep one other crop type growing so you can pick them up immediately after reset and progress toward the next reset.
If the tech fails, check crop depot; you may not have pushed growth speed far enough via night market.
Need speed GMO (growth speed from thousands of certain crops) and super GMO buff stat around 100k for the tech to work.
Tech transfers previous growth speed to current run and uncaps the 7-hour hard cap on metals; with nothing to transfer, it won't work.
Don't do other resets, re-zoning, daily reset waiting, or going to hole; only go to bean guy, hand in ticket, return to world 6 town.
Need somewhat progressed night market and decent growth speed because there must be something to transfer to metal crops.
Community is split on whether the metal crop tech is a bug exploit or tech; he says it's probably the most controversial tech.
If widely discussed it's information and thus tech; only the developer's opinion matters, and if dev calls it an exploit don't do it.
Tech has been in the game for about a year or longer; maybe since start of 4.7.
Compares metal crop tech to other unintended behavior treated as tech in IdleOn; says it is the same or better.
Top platform tech for AC (spitting out four skulls) is unintended behavior yet considered tech.
DB Colosseum tech forcing mobs to spawn in the corner is likely unintended but seen as tech.
If developer says it's bad don't do it, if fine do it, if silent it's fine until proven otherwise; he favors sharing knowledge.
Tech has been in the game roughly a year; not a niche bug known by three people so no need to report.
